candidates.why: _buf is allocated at 1176 (alloca, which is malloc under the HAVE_ALLOCA fallback per myalloca.h:47), then reassigned at 1184 to cquote()'s return. In the len>255 && dxf==1 branch the loop advances the pointer with `_buf += 255` at 1199, so by the time freea(_buf) runs at 1206 it frees an interior pointer, not the original allocation. With freea==free (myalloca.h:49) this is an invalid free / heap corruption; the original block is also leaked.

At 1184 `_buf = cquote(_buf, len, str)` overwrites the pointer returned by alloca at 1176 with cquote's return value. cquote returns `d` (== dest, the same base) at 1151, so normally identical, but the code then frees whatever cquote returned at 1206 while the original alloca'd block (if cquote ever returned a different pointer) would be leaked and the wrong pointer freed. Suspicious aliasing of the freed object.

created_by is a file-scope global (line 69) assigned from json_string() (ATTRIBUTE_MALLOC) at 828. It is freed at 4305 and only NULLed at 4306 on the success path. All early-return paths (4194, 4201, 4225, 4232, 4242, 4289, 4295) return without freeing or clearing it, so a second dwg_read_json call can free a pointer already freed by a previous successful call (double-free / use-after-free of the global).

On the jsmn error path at 4194 tokens.tokens is freed and the function returns, but the global created_by (set at 828 in a prior call) is left dangling; a later call reaching free(created_by) at 4305 frees a stale pointer. Cross-call lifetime of the global is not reset on error paths.
